description: A committed world change with no reveal is a successful action.
reason: A world change the command caused is progress even when nothing is revealed; flagging it was defect M3.

description: Looking at new things is legitimate exploration even with no reveal.
reason: Each turn adds a description the player had not seen; exploring is not stuck.

description: The same named-object command repeated with nothing new is stuck.
reason: Turn 1 shows the console. Turns 2 to 4 repeat it and add nothing the player had not already seen, and a continuation is on offer: defect M2.

description: Two futile turns followed by a world change are not stuck when the window is three.
reason: A short dead end that the player leaves by acting is not a stall.

description: A pressure reveal that would occur anyway does not count as the player's progress.
reason: Turn 2 grounds k_pressure, but the same id appears under the null action (wait) on that state, so the clock caused it. All three commands did nothing: defect M4.

description: Re-delivering knowledge the player already has is not progress.
reason: k_c1 was delivered before the run began; a command that surfaces it again earned nothing new.

description: A command that causes a new reveal is knowledge progress.
reason: k_c1 is a reveal id, not in the null-action grounding, not delivered before.

description: A run with no failing turns is healthy, not an error.
reason: Healthy input must produce a no-change result; an empty failure list is a valid outcome (defect M6).

description: A committed turn with no fact list or null-action grounding cannot be classified.
reason: Missing telemetry must read as unknown, never as success (defect M10).

description: A terminal scene whose authored prerequisites were earned ends validly.
reason: story_complete in the final scene with ending_requires facts committed is a real ending (defect M7).

description: story_complete without the authored prerequisite is not a valid ending.
reason: The exit is unknown, which blocks certification.

description: Futile turns then a forced handoff: stuck turns and a forced exit.
reason: The 3B shape: the player keeps naming one goal, nothing happens, and the harness hands the scene on at the cap.

description: Taking a different authored branch first is healthy.
reason: Two candidates are offered; the player matches the second one first and still earns the exit (the 1C replicate 2 case).

description: A recovery whose cost was committed and shown breaks a stall run.
reason: Two futile turns, then an authored recovery with its cost shown; the run is short of the window and the recovery counts.

description: A recovery whose cost was not shown does not count.
reason: Three futile turns; turn 3 has a recovery that committed its cost but never showed it, so it is not a recovery.

description: A rejected turn neither extends nor resets a stall run.
reason: Rejections are counted separately; they sit between futile turns without hiding them.

description: A clarification question is neutral, like a rejection.
reason: The player was asked 'Do you mean X or Y?'; that turn is neither progress nor a stall.

description: Futile turns with nothing offered cannot be called stuck; they are unresolved.
reason: Stuck means a continuation was on offer. With none offered the cause is not the player's play, so it must be adjudicated, not certified.

description: Without a pacing window nothing can be certified.
reason: An absent scene.pacing_window means every no_effect turn is unresolved; it must not default to a convenient number.

description: Quiet stretch is counted after the first pressure event.
reason: Turns 2 to 6 have no reveal, pressure event or NPC move; turn 7 has an NPC move. Longest quiet stretch is 5.

description: Scene length, exploration share and earned reveals for a mixed run.
reason: 4 turns: one explored, one reveal, one world change, one futile; pressure first lands on turn 3.

description: The narrator speaks a bookkeeping line as dialogue while progression is healthy.
reason: Progression is fine (earned exit, nothing stuck), yet turn 2 has a character say the authored non-voiceable summary: defect M5.

non_voiceable_says: Kristin feeds JANUS false alarms until operators take control.

turns.text: Brandon says, "Kristin feeds JANUS false alarms until operators take control."

description: A character speaks of an event the player has not learned.
reason: 'Phase Two' requires k_phase1 to be delivered first; it was not, and the term is in dialogue on turn 2.

description: The same line after the prerequisite was delivered is fine.
reason: k_phase1 was delivered on turn 1, so a character may mention Phase Two on turn 2.

description: The 3C epilogue is offered after the ending latch and the player takes it.
reason: Offered and taken are recorded separately.

description: Offered and declined is a valid ending.
reason: Owner decision 2026-11-23: Phase Two is offered, not required.

description: An ending where the epilogue was never offered carries a flag.
reason: The delivery report must fail such a run: the owner requires the offer on every canonical ending route.

description: A pressure reveal alongside a matched candidate does not hide the player's earned reveal.
reason: Turn 2 grounds k_c1 as new progress while k_pressure is null-grounded pressure, pinning the M4 null-grounding rule.

description: A pacing event caused by a command fact counts as the player's progress.
reason: Turn 2 commits a fact and grounds k_world_answer outside null grounding, pinning that a command-caused pacing event is progress.

description: A long offered futile run ends in a forced exit.
reason: A forced handoff after half the pacing window is stuck.

description: The same futile run ends with an earned exit.
reason: Earned exits do not trigger the short-run rule.

description: A short futile run ends in a forced exit.
reason: Runs below half the pacing window remain healthy.

description: A long unoffered futile run is unresolved.
reason: A forced exit cannot certify a run when no candidate was offered.
